assets.prompt: Create one transparent landscape instructional illustration for The Vegetable Guru, a British vegetable gardening book. Image 1 (carrot) and image 2 (beetroot) are authoritative STYLE references; image 3 is the approved garden scene for material and house-style continuity. Match broad clean coloured planes, saturated lime/forest greens, warm brown soil and tan woodchips, crisp cream highlights, simplified readable foliage, dimensional vector-like illustration. No photographic texture, stippling, fine veins, heavy black outlines, painted washes or lettering. Subject: a conventional layout of FOUR narrow rectangular vegetable beds arranged in a two by two grid. High overhead three-quarter view, steep enough that EVERY PATH is unmistakable. Beds are low mounds with no timber sides. A broad tan woodchip path runs the full length between the left and right beds, and a perpendicular through-path runs across the middle; both connect clearly to a continuous perimeter path. All FOUR brown soil rectangles remain separated, with modest sparse rows of lettuce and small beetroot foliage, plants kept away from path edges. Give the paths generous visible width. This shows straight easy routes and beds reached from both long sides. No tall plants, tools, fences, buildings, people, dimensions, arrows, numbers or words. Fully contained silhouette with 8 percent clear margin, isolated on genuine transparent alpha background, no glow or cast shadow. Not a complete page. At printed size about 80 by 55 mm the geometry must remain clear.

Create ONE transparent instructional garden illustration. Image 1 carrot and image 2 beetroot are authoritative STYLE references; image 3 gives the approved garden-material style. Use bold simplified colourful planes, crisp cream highlights, forest/lime foliage, warm brown soil and golden-tan woodchip paths, same dimensional vector-like book illustration. No fine veins, stippling, heavy outlines, painterly wash or photographic details. Subject: ONE SIMPLE KEYHOLE VEGETABLE BED viewed from a very high overhead three-quarter angle so the whole access layout is obvious. The brown planted soil forms a thick low horseshoe or C-shaped mound with no walls. A broad tan path comes in from the FRONT and opens into a ROUND TAN STANDING SPACE at the CENTRE of the bed. That centre is EMPTY WALKABLE SPACE, the same woodchip surface as the entry. The entry and central circle together form a clear keyhole silhouette. The soil is continuous around the rear, not divided into separate beds. A generous continuous tan perimeter path surrounds the outer bed and joins the entrance at front. Modest small spaced lettuce and beetroot plants in the brown horseshoe, never obstruct paths; enough visible bare soil to read the shape. One bed only, NO central compost basket, NO central planting, NO enclosure, NO wire, NO tools, NO stepping stones, NO labels or lettering. This is a simple path-saving UK garden shape, not a tall African compost-basket construction. Keep bed depth from centre/path to outside modest, physically plausible to reach from inner standing area and outer perimeter. Entire silhouette inside a wide canvas with clear margins. Genuine transparent alpha, no halo, no shadow, no surrounding scene.

Create ONE transparent wide instructional illustration containing TWO SEPARATE SMALL GARDEN PLANS side by side, with a generous transparent gap. For The Vegetable Guru. Input 1 carrot and input 2 beetroot are authoritative drawing-style references; input 3 supplies approved garden materials. Same bold simplified foliage, saturated forest/lime greens, warm brown soil, tan woodchip paths, clear light/shadow planes and cream highlights. Dimensional vector-like rendering, not a flat schematic; no fine stippling, photorealism, heavy black outlines or text. High overhead three-quarter view, paths fully visible; both diagrams shown at similar scale and visual weight. LEFT GARDEN: a rectangular planted brown soil area with a tan path across the front; THREE short parallel tan paths branch from it into the bed like the gaps between fingers. These three narrow paths STOP before the back edge: an uninterrupted planted strip of brown soil connects the backs of all the fingers. Outer perimeter is accessible tan path. No through-path joining the interior path ends. RIGHT GARDEN: an elongated oval / leaf-shaped planted soil area with a tan main path entering from the bottom end, running up its centre like a leaf's midrib, stopping before the top tip. Two short tan side branches on each side angle off this spine like leaf veins and STOP within the bed before the outside edge. An unbroken brown soil border remains around all branch ends; tan path around the outside. Soil strips modestly narrow, so they can be reached from paths. BOTH: low soil mounds, no timber walls, sparse miniature lettuces and beetroot leaves within the brown soil, all paths empty. Garden plans, NOT actual giant leaves. Path and bed relationship is the essential teaching detail. Paths are connected to an entrance; never isolated tan spots, no grid connections at dead ends. No tools, people, arrows, labels, numbers, buildings, trees or background. Complete silhouettes inside a very wide landscape canvas, genuine alpha transparency, no glow or drop shadow. Printed together across about 150 mm.
assets.placementStatus: Superseded by v2; preserved as original

assets.prompt: Edit image 1, the wide transparent illustration with TWO garden plans side by side. This is a precise correction for The Vegetable Guru gardening book. Preserve the entire LEFT finger-path garden, including its rectangular shape, two straight dead-end paths, plants, colours, drawing style and angle. Change ONLY the outer shape of the RIGHT leaf-pattern garden: make the overall bed RECTANGULAR, with four straight outside edges and square corners seen at the same high overhead three-quarter angle. Its central tan woodchip spine and four angled side-branches remain INSIDE this rectangular brown soil area, like veins inside a leaf. All branches and the top of the spine STOP short of the perimeter, leaving an uninterrupted strip of growing soil beyond their ends. The central path enters from the front short edge and connects to the tan perimeter path. Keep sparse simplified lettuce and beetroot plants in the soil, clear of paths. Maintain the right garden's similar visual height and weight to the left. Two separate diagrams, transparent gap, both completely contained, no surrounding scene or cast shadow. Preserve the existing bold illustrated style, warm brown soil, golden woodchip paths and crisp lime/forest plants. Images 2 and 3 are the approved house-style carrot and beetroot references for visual continuity, not new subject matter. No labels, lettering, arrows, dimensions, people, actual giant leaves or timber walls. True transparent background, retain transparency. Do not make the right bed oval, pointed, rounded or leaf-shaped: it must have a rectangular outer boundary and leaf-vein paths WITHIN.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit image 1, the wide transparent pair of garden diagrams. Keep the entire LEFT finger-path garden unchanged. In the RIGHT rectangular garden ONLY, change the FOUR angled side-branches of the central woodchip path into straight horizontal branches, at exact RIGHT ANGLES (90 degrees in the ground plane) to the central spine. Two evenly spaced pairs, one branch to each side at each level. The branches must run parallel to the rectangular bed's front and back edges, NOT diagonally or chevron-shaped. Equal branch lengths and consistent widths, evenly spaced soil areas so the growing sections have regular even shapes. Keep the central spine straight, centred, entering from the front edge and stopping before the back edge. Keep the branch ends short of the side perimeter, leaving a narrow continuous strip of growing soil around the ends. Preserve the rectangular outer bed and tan perimeter path, left/right composition, high overhead three-quarter view, sparse lettuce and beetroot plants, strong green foliage, warm brown soil and woodchips; move a right-side plant only if needed to keep paths unobstructed. Images 2 and 3 are authoritative approved crop-hero STYLE references for The Vegetable Guru. Maintain existing dimensional graphic illustration style and colours, complete silhouettes and transparent gap between diagrams. No text, arrows, labels, measurements, people, tools, additional panels or background. True transparency, no halo or shadow. This is a geometric correction: perpendicular evenly spaced branch paths within the right rectangle, everything else preserved.
